evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep: 'This would take within the next five to ten minutes of your time. Would that be okay?' — time-boxed and promise of quote present, but framing was rushed and abbreviated ('basically we just wanted to ask you some information in order for us to check and give you an accurate quote').
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep: 'I just wanted to check if you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today.' — asked AFTER the customer had already stated name and location. Probing had begun in the form of confirming the first address before this question.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer states 'No, just the quote' — no concerns raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covered: property type (two-story house both locations), bedrooms (2 at origin, 3.5 at destination), rooms (living room, kitchen noted), parking (driveway at origin, street at destination), access concerns asked, special items (washer/dryer), and packing needs.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep: 'So a typical back count based on your home size is 45 to 55 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?' — asked, and customer engaged on this.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided anchored estimate: '...in your case, we're coming from a two story house going to the new location which is like, less than ten minutes away...two movers and one truck estimated time is between three to four hours to partially pack your items. Then on the following day...two movers and one truck estimated time is between six to seven hours...' Then personalized: 'I just wanted to let you know that in case if we are doing packing and moving, if they end up four hours on the first day, seven hours on the following day, the total estimate that we have would be $2,436.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep disclosed: '$101 per hour per mover, minimum of two ($204), 2.5-hour minimum prorated to 15-minute increments, no hidden fees (no credit card fees, no sterile fees, no disassemble/reassembly fees), packing cost of $200 for partial packing with materials included, no deposit required.' — full transparency and commitment framing delivered.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. Rep moved directly from estimate explanation into discussing move day logistics without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or pausing for customer reaction.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep: 'We will provide up to $2,000 per move that is to repair, replace and reimburse for your items...for protection like in case there and there is any mishaps or any accidental damages.' — coverage amount and purpose stated, but the no-deductible / no-fine-print framing was absent. Customer asked 'So take the $2,000 just for what?' and rep clarified it was for protection, but the 'built into the rate, not an add-on' and 'no deductible' framing was never delivered.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep: 'We also have on time guarantee. So we value your time if you cannot on time guarantee...if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we start discounting money of your final bill and we will also send you emails beforehand letting you know who would be your movers...' — discount terms and email preview mentioned, fully delivered.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep asked: 'Do you still have any queries or concerns that you want me to add to address before I let you go.' — genuine loop-close attempt without repeating prior content.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep: 'Do you still have any queries or concerns that you want me to add to address before I let you go.' — phrased as 'queries or concerns,' which is closer to the rubric's genuine version, but customer response was 'No, I think that's really helpful,' so effectiveness is unclear. However, this is NOT the empty 'any questions?' throwaway; it's a genuine ask.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No recognizable version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' was present.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep: 'Would you like our help with your move?' — asked plainly with no built-in out. Customer: 'Yes, I can.' Clear acceptance.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep: 'No recent securing your spot. If something comes up or change in your end then you can always reschedule or can cancel with a quick call, no fees for that either.' — no explicit 'rate lock' terminology, but the 'no deposit required' and flexibility framing covers the substance.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirmed: date/time window (Saturday 8:30 AM–9:00 AM to pack, Sunday the 25th to move), arrival window, no deposit. Missing: explicit phone number confirmation, crew size (implied as two movers, but not explicitly confirmed at booking), addresses (already gathered but not read back at booking confirmation), and crew notes about customer's prep priorities.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details across both properties and packing preferences, delivered full pricing transparency with clear fee structure and no-hidden-fees framing, and closed with an explicit ask that secured the booking.
coaching_note: Section 4: ask 'Does that feel fair?' and hold genuine silence before moving into move-day logistics; Section 2: ask the agenda question ('What are your biggest concerns?') BEFORE diving into property details; Section 5: add explicit 'no deductible, no fine print' framing when covering the $2,000 damage coverage; Section 6: include the catch-all ('Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?') before the final ask.
